newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on USDA export data, soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on USDA export data, soy.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a bullish USDA weekly export sales report and gains in soybeans, traders said.
USDA Friday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended May 22 totalled 1,002,900 tonnes, above expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Support also came from slow farmer selling and mostly firm cash basis markets, traders said.
But gains were limited by good crop weather in the U.S. Midwest.
U.S. corn planting was near a record pace and forecasts for warmer weather in the Midwest will boost production prospects.
Corn closed 1/2 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 1-1/2 at $2.70-3/4. December closed 3/4 higher at $2.54.
Smith Barney bought five million bushels of July, Refco Inc bought three million July and Prudential Securities bought two million July, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold three million bushels of December and Cargill Investor Services sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 57,000 contracts, below the 70,526 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Iowa Grain bought 400 December $2.60 calls at 14-1/4 to 15 cents and sold 400 December $2.30 puts at five cents, traders said. Prudential Securities bought 250 December $3.00 puts at 49-1/2 to 50-1/4 cents and USA Trading bought 300 July $3.50 calls at 1/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, above the 13,930 traded Thursday.
